command: set -e; cd /code; yarn --frozen-lockfile; fp="$BACKEND|$OSF_URL|$OSF_API_URL|$CAS_URL|$OSF_RENDER_URL|$OSF_FILE_URL|$OSF_HELP_URL|$OSF_COOKIE_DOMAIN"; if [ ! -f /code/dist/index.html ] || [ "$(cat /code/dist/.grdm-build 2>/dev/null)" != "$fp" ]; then echo "ember: building dist for $fp"; rm -rf /code/dist/*; node_modules/.bin/ember build --environment development --output-path /code/dist; printf %s "$fp" > /code/dist/.grdm-build; fi; exec node_modules/.bin/ember serve --path /code/dist --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4200 --live-reload false
note: ember-osf-web's config/environment.js takes its backend URLs from the environment (OSF_URL, OSF_API_URL, OSF_RENDER_URL, OSF_FILE_URL, OSF_HELP_URL, CAS_URL, OSF_COOKIE_DOMAIN); the defaults are localhost:<port> and the retired alias 192.168.168.167:8080 for CAS, so every value is set from the published loopback ports (ADR-02). The prebuilt image runs `ember server`, a full ember-cli build at every start that takes 10+ minutes under amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon and was OOM-killed twice at 6.3 GiB (real install runs 10-12); the command therefore builds once into the named volume ember_osf_web_dist (/code/dist) with a fingerprint of the URL settings in /code/dist/.grdm-build, rebuilds only when that fingerprint changes, and serves the prebuilt output with `ember serve --path`. Live reload is off (no 41953 port): edit-and-reload of ember sources is not a goal of the prebuilt fallback; it returns with the M4 Dockerfile. JOBS=2 caps ember-cli's parallel build workers; weight 4 and at least 8 GiB cover the build.
